First off let me say I mean no foul to the kid in terms of accomplishing something, but in light of this thing blowing up the way it did, this should be said. He got arrested for something that he can't really claim as his own work. Let me explain...

The clock in question

After I got a better look at the so called clock the kid "made" that got him arrested, I noticed something interesting. I got curious as to why this kid designed and built a clock that was powered, obviously, by an AC transformer that also had a 9 volt battery snap. After that I noticed that this was not some Arduino or other microcontroller powered clock like I was expecting. There are two circuit boards joined by a ribbon cable. The boards are pretty crappy in quality and machine soldered. The ribbon cable quality is the type common in cheap consumer electronics. If you are familiar at all with the guts of a digital alarm clock, you will notice that this device is exactly that. The transformer powers the clock from AC and the 9 volt battery is the backup for when the power fails. The secondary circuit board (longer of the two) is the one with the buttons for the controls and the main board has the clock chip that runs it all. This kid literally took apart a standard alarm clock and sort of half-assed mounted it in a separate box. Now I'm not trying to dismiss the kid, but since he landed himself a potential trip to see the POTUS, having taken credit for a much lesser accomplishment makes this whole thing crazier than it already is. I can see the kid not wanting to fess up to what his work was, but I don't want to see people blow smoke up his ass for something not truly as amazing as it's been billed as by some. I've seen younger kids do actual projects that are their own work not get the praise they deserve so let's not pretend this is his credit. If anything the credit goes to some Chinese engineer who designed a cheaply made alarm clock.
